page: Microsoft Azure E20ads_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Eadv6 server family. It is powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V74 processor running at 3.7 GHz, featuring 10 physical cores and 20 vCPUs via hyperthreading on the x86_64 architecture. The hardware configuration includes 160.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Storage is bundled with a 1181 GB local disk, and the instance is premium storage capable.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 25%. Memory subsystem performance is also strong, as reflected in the Passmark memory score. Multi-core operations, including stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and Passmark CPU scores, fall within the average range. The server demonstrates average memory bandwidth for both cached and uncached read/write operations, alongside average performance in database operations, Redis SET operations, and static web serving.

While the server excels in single-threaded tasks and text processing, it exhibits performance tradeoffs in large-scale workloads. For instance, LLM inference prompt processing for large 70B models is weak, falling into the bottom 25%, whereas text generation for small 135M models is strong. Given the high memory density, dedicated CPU allocation, and substantial local storage, this server is well-suited for memory-intensive workloads, database hosting, text processing, and moderate-scale web serving, offering balanced resource density and qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound applications.
